The independent reviewer’s conclusion is supported in its limited form: D397 and D436 do not provide a general procedure for choosing the main part whenever an outcome names several things. The review is one reading of descriptions and outcomes, without the full articles or requests. Its **29** are therefore cases this reviewer could not settle from those inputs, not 29 proven product ambiguities or 29 decisions Alex must make. The **63 of 66** count includes settlement sources and comparisons; it answers a different question from the earlier count of about 30 and should not replace it as though the two measured the same thing. [Independent review]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/rule-review.md:1), [review instructions]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/rule-review-prompt.md:9)

For D580 and Alex’s page, I would say: **“The attempted change listed more omitted parts but also produced two refusals both readers considered unjustified. We have no reviewed repair: the records do not give a general rule for identifying the main part in every multi-part topic.”** Keep the result’s strict-count H and XR regressions beside that statement. “Listing fixed” overstates a small selected probe with two refused answers. [Probe result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/unlisted-parts/RESULT.md:3)

D439 does allow the council to take a reversible product choice while Alex is away; D544 expressly withdrew an earlier deferral for that reason. It does **not** supply evidence for an arbitrary main-part rule, or authority to contradict an existing decision. Here, the record supports keeping A stopped, but does not establish that every possible compliant repair or council decision is exhausted. Deck 1 and the six lines’ role remain in the recorded order for Alex. [D439]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4871), [D544]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:6616), [current state]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:323)

The next bounded, reversible step I would consider is **a $0 check of the Idea planner against a stored new-system library**, without opening a live service or making a model call. This remains a separate integration item, not something D575 paused. The page contract already says a composite is unavailable when an undirected new-system question is a driver; the planner currently maps the first and last choices as endpoints, which for a three-choice event can mean Yes and Still open. Trace a stored event, an undirected range and a directed company figure through the planner and its consumer using recorded or synthetic responses. **Falsifier:** the planner already preserves those shapes without assigning a direction or computing a misleading composite. If the mismatch holds, return with a narrow design and its product consequences; this would advance integration, **not pass a quality gate**. [Page contract]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/DESIGN.md:16), [planner]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/idea_composite.py:90), [D575]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7377)

Hold further paid work on the stopped line. Do not present the absence of a candidate today as proof that no reversible council-owned work remains.

CONSENSUS: no, because the review does not make all 29 cases Alex-only decisions, and the separate Idea-planner integration check remains available at $0.
